sections.h2: Which Carteret County office handles property tax?
sections.html:
Carteret County runs assessing and collecting out of a single Tax Administration office, led by an appointed Tax Administrator. The commissioners make the appointment, and the administrator also reports on legal compliance to state bodies in Raleigh.

Walk-in service is on the first floor of the Administration Building, 302 Courthouse Square in Beaufort, and at a Western Office on Cedar Point Blvd. in Cedar Point (701 Cedar Point Blvd., NC 28584). The phone is 252-728-8485, and weekday hours at both are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., holidays excepted. Office staff also serve the review board that hears value appeals.

Its stated job covers appraisal, assessment, billing and collection of tax on real, business and personal property, plus keeping the records the state Department of Revenue asks for. A seller can ask this office what is owed on a parcel and whether a relief claim is on file.

sections.h2: When are Carteret County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The bill falls due on September 1, but interest does not begin until January 6 of the next year. From then the county charges 2% for January and 0.75% for each later month.

The county's August 2026 release puts the fiscal year 2026-27 rate at 22.5 cents per $100 of assessed value. Real and personal property get separate bills. Property in Beaufort, Bogue, Cape Carteret, Cedar Point, Emerald Isle, Morehead City or Peletier receives a single bill with county and town tax combined. A mailed check is credited as of its postmark.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Carteret County assessed value?
sections.html:
Submit the Real Property Appeal Form to the Tax Administration Office within the window on your value notice. For a reappraisal notice the county sets that window at 30 days from the notice date, and it limits appeals to the assessed value, ruling out arguments about the rate or the bill.

The county's last general reappraisal used a January 1, 2025 market value, and its notice tells owners to compare their property's characteristics and comparable sales against what was used. The assessor is presumed to have acted in good faith, so the burden sits with the owner. Evidence that helps: sales of similar nearby homes, damage photos and repair quotes.

  • First level: the Board of Equalization and Review, nine local residents counting two alternates, which mails its Notice of Decision within a month of meeting.
  • Second level: the state Property Tax Commission, which you reach by filing within 30 days of that notice. Hearings are typically in Raleigh, and a lawyer may be needed.
  • Third level: the North Carolina Court of Appeals, only on a question of law, and then the state Supreme Court.

Boats, aircraft, mobile homes and business equipment follow a different path: file within 30 days of the date on the annual bill, and the county sets a conference before issuing a final decision. The result can go down, up or stay put, and it applies only from that year onward. Statewide, G.S. 105-290 sets the 30-day window to reach the Property Tax Commission.

sections.h2: What property tax relief can a Carteret County owner claim?
sections.html:
North Carolina offers three ways to cut a home's bill, and an owner can take only one. The county tax office takes the application, not the state.

  • Age or disability: the owner must be 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, with 2026 income no higher than $38,800. A qualifying owner has the larger of $25,000 or half the value taken off the taxable base.
  • Veteran exclusion: $45,000 of appraised value comes off for a qualifying disabled veteran or unmarried surviving spouse, and the state form lists no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: the cap on the bill is 4.0% of income, rising to 5.0% for incomes above $38,800 and up to $58,200. Five years of owning and living in the home come first, and the excess tax is deferred rather than forgiven.

The application is Form AV-9. File it during the January listing period if you can, because the assessor must accept it until June 1. A circuit breaker claim must be renewed yearly, and a sale, a death or a move triggers repayment of the deferred amounts for the three prior years. Carteret's delinquent tax page steers older, disabled and veteran owners toward these programs. Read the statutes at G.S. 105-277.1, 105-277.1B and 105-277.1C.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Carteret County tax bill?
sections.html:
Four routes work: the web portal, the phone line, the mail and the counter. The portal accepts cards, eCheck and PayPal, while 1-888-544-9433 takes card payments if you have the bill in hand.

  • Mail: a check payable to County of Carteret, sent to PO Box 96264, Charlotte, NC 28296-6264.
  • Counter: Beaufort or Cedar Point, paying by cash, check, money order or card.
  • Drop box: at the courthouse entrance, no cash, processed the next business day.

Fees apply to cards. The county's payment page prints a $1.50 flat charge for an eCheck and 2.50% plus $0.30 a transaction on credit cards. Partial payments in any amount are allowed online, but the full balance must be in before delinquency, and the county's news release says the phone line does not take partial amounts. An owner who cannot pay in full can apply for a hardship payment arrangement. Interest keeps running under it, but it may lower the odds of garnishment or foreclosure.

sections.h2: What happens when Carteret County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The lien on the parcel stays, interest keeps growing, and the county can use enforcement tools. G.S. 105-355 fixes the lien to the parcel as of the listing date, with penalties, interest and costs riding along.

The county lists wage and bank garnishment, state income tax refund setoff, setoff against lottery winnings, attachment of rent, seizure and sale of personal property, and foreclosure on real property. The foreclosure route, in G.S. 105-374, resembles a mortgage foreclosure and ends at an auction on the courthouse steps, followed by a commissioner's report and a ten-day window for higher bids. Redemption stays open until confirmation, at the price of the taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

A sale before that point is usually cleaner. According to the county, the advertisement of a delinquent account starts the advanced foreclosure process, so an owner who is behind should call 252-728-8485 before the March 1 to June 30 publication period.

sections.h2: How does a sale affect a Carteret County tax bill?
sections.html:
A tax balance follows the parcel as a lien, so it is normally cleared at closing. Request a current figure from the Tax Administration Office, and agree with the closing attorney how this year's bill is divided.

Filing the deed is a separate errand at the register of deeds, covered on our Carteret County register of deeds page. If a circuit breaker deferral is on the property, the deferred taxes for the preceding three years become due on a transfer.

Census QuickFacts puts Carteret County at 70,469 residents on July 1, 2025, with 54,293 housing units. Across 2020-2024 the median owned home was valued at $333,300, 74.7% of units were owner-occupied, and 30.1% of residents were 65 or older. The data is on the Census Bureau page for Carteret County.

faqs.q: What is the Carteret County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The 2026-27 county rate is 22.5 cents per $100, per the county's August 2026 release. Parcels inside a town add the town rate and arrive on one combined bill.

faqs.q: When do Carteret County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On January 6, following the September 1 due date. A payment through January 5 owes no interest; after that comes 2% for January and 0.75% for each month beyond.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Carteret County assessment?
faqs.a: Real property owners have thirty days from the change of value notice, and personal property owners have thirty days from the bill date. Only value is open to challenge.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Carteret County tax bill in person?
faqs.a: Visit the Beaufort office or the Western Office in Cedar Point, both open weekdays from 8 a.m. until 5 p.m. A drop box at the courthouse entrance accepts checks.

faqs.q: Can Carteret County set up a payment plan?
faqs.a: Yes, in limited cases. The county offers a hardship payment arrangement by application and lets owners pay in partial amounts before delinquency. A plan does not stop interest from running.
